papers.title: Delaying rewards reduces egoism bias during prosocial acts.
papers.abstract: People tend to prioritize their own benefits over those of others during reward evaluation, a tendency known as egoism bias. Recent evidence suggests that delaying rewards may reduce this bias in prosocial behavior, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated this issue by recording EEG activity when participants (N = 40) evaluated immediate or delayed rewards for themselves and an anonymous person during a prosocial reward task. We found an egoism bias in immediate reward evaluation, with stronger preferences and neural reward sensitivity (as indexed by the reward positivity, P3, and delta power) for self-benefiting compared to other-benefiting trials. Crucially, this egoism bias decreases when rewards were delayed, as shown by comparable reward sensitivity, overlapping neural representations, and positive neural correlations between self-benefiting and other-benefiting trials. These convergent findings establish reward deferral as a critical variable in reducing egoism bias during prosocial decision-making.
papers.summary: 本研究探討延遲獎勵如何影響親社會行為中的利己主義偏見。透過記錄40名參與者在評估即時或延遲的自身與他人獎勵時的腦電圖（EEG）發現，在即時獎勵評估中存在顯著的利己主義偏見，表現為對自身獲益試驗有更強的偏好與神經獎勵敏感性（如獎賞正波、P3及delta功率）。然而，當獎勵被延遲時，這種利己主義偏見顯著降低，自身與他人獲益試驗之間的獎勵敏感性變得相當，且神經表徵出現重疊與正相關。
papers.significance: 此研究首次從神經科學角度證實，延遲獎勵是減少親社會決策中利己主義偏見的關鍵變數。這不僅揭示了延遲獎勵降低利己偏見的潛在神經機制（即拉近了自我與他人獲益的神經表徵），也為促進合作、利他行為及相關政策設計（如強調長期收益而非短期利益）提供了重要的理論基礎與實務啟示。
